name: Chronic wasting disease in deer with environmental prion accumulation
description:
Chronic wasting disease (prion), mule deer / white-tailed deer.
Only 3 compartments, which makes this the cleanest demonstration of an environmental-reservoir model: with beta_env = 0 the epidemic is density-dependent and self-limiting, while with slow prion decay the environmental term creates a ratche
Parameter values: 0 of 10 checked against the source; the rest are recalled or illustrative.
reference: Miller MW, Hobbs NT, Tavener SJ (2006). Dynamics of prion disease transmission in mule deer. Ecological Applications 16(6):2208–2214

compartments.name: Ii
compartments.description: infected deer (long subclinical + clinical infection, assumed infectious throughout)

compartments.name: Ev
compartments.description: environmental prion load (infectious units; E avoided for clarity)

parameters.name: beta_dir
parameters.description: direct deer-to-deer transmission coefficient (density-dependent) [illustrative] (per deer per year)

parameters.name: beta_env
parameters.description: environment-to-deer transmission coefficient [illustrative] (per prion unit per year)

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: CWD-induced mortality rate (mean time from infection to death ≈2 years) [unverified] (per year)

parameters.name: shed
parameters.description: shedding from live infected animals (saliva, urine, faeces) [illustrative] (prion units per infected deer per year)

parameters.name: carc
parameters.description: prion deposited by a carcass [illustrative] (prion units per CWD death)

parameters.name: decay_e
parameters.description: loss of environmental infectivity (prions persist for years; this is the parameter the literature identifies as pivotal) [illustrative] (per year)

parameters.name: harvest
parameters.description: hunter harvest rate (control lever; can be applied preferentially to Ii) [illustrative] (per year)
